dublinCore.title: Fourier Series Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Fourier Series
Fourier Coefficients
Harmonics
Gibbs Phenomenon
dublinCore.description: Build square, triangle, sawtooth, pulse-train and hand-drawn periodic waveforms from their first N harmonics. A time plot overlays the partial sum on the waveform, and bar charts show the amplitude and phase of each harmonic or the cosine and sine coefficients.

learningObjectives: Explain a Fourier series as a sum of harmonics of the fundamental frequency
Compare the harmonic content of square, triangle, sawtooth and pulse waveforms
Describe how the partial sum converges as harmonics are added, and what the Gibbs phenomenon is
Relate the coefficients a_n and b_n to the amplitude and phase of each harmonic
Predict from the symmetry of a waveform whether its series has cosine terms, sine terms or both

misconceptions.misconception: Adding enough harmonics removes the overshoot at a jump
misconceptions.correction: The rms error goes to zero, but the peak of the ripple stays at about 9% of the jump height (the Gibbs phenomenon)
misconceptions.evidence: Step the square wave from N = 9 to N = 50: the rms error in the banner falls from 0.201 to 0.090 while the overshoot stays at about 9%

misconceptions.misconception: Every periodic waveform contains every harmonic
misconceptions.correction: The harmonic content depends on the waveform and its symmetry; some harmonics have zero amplitude
misconceptions.evidence: The square wave has zero amplitude at every even n, and the 25% duty-cycle pulse train has no bar at n = 4, 8, 12

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A periodic waveform and the sum of its first N Fourier harmonics drawn over two periods, with bar charts of the amplitude and phase of each harmonic. Buttons step the number of harmonics up and down.

visualElements.description: Time plot over two periods: waveform (grey), partial sum (red) and the selected harmonic (orange); drag in it to draw the custom waveform
Magnitude spectrum bars and phase spectrum stems, or a_n and b_n bar charts; hover selects a harmonic and a click switches it off
Banner with the rms error and the Gibbs overshoot, and a readout of the selected harmonic's coefficients

model.description: Partial sum of the first N terms of the Fourier series of a periodic waveform, with its rms error and Gibbs overshoot
equations: x(t) = a0 + sum over n of [a_n cos(n w0 t) + b_n sin(n w0 t)], w0 = 2 pi / T
c_n = (a_n - j b_n) / 2, amplitude = sqrt(a_n^2 + b_n^2) = 2 |c_n|
square wave: b_n = 4 / (pi n) for odd n
triangle wave: b_n = 8 (-1)^((n-1)/2) / (pi^2 n^2) for odd n
pulse train with duty cycle d: a0 = d, a_n = 2 sin(pi n d) / (pi n)

variables.name: N
variables.description: Number of harmonics in the partial sum

variables.name: rmsError
variables.description: rms difference between the waveform and the partial sum over one period

variables.name: overshoot
variables.description: How far the highest peak or lowest trough of the partial sum lies beyond the waveform, as a fraction of the jump height

instructionalStrategies: Step-through synthesis: add one harmonic at a time and compare the partial sum with the waveform
Record overshoot and rms error for increasing N and explain the trend
extensions: Draw a custom waveform with both even and odd symmetry and compare its a_n and b_n
Compare the convergence rate of a waveform with a jump and one without
